measures.methodNote: Additive log-mean Divisia (LMDI-I) shift-share on CMS-64 benefit spending S = sum over groups of E_g x c_g, with E = full-year-equivalent enrollees and c = spending per enrollee, for two groups (newly eligible adults; all other). Each group's change is split exactly into enrollment = L(S1,S0)*ln(E1/E0), mix = L*ln(share1/share0), cost = L*ln(c1/c0), where L(a,b)=(a-b)/ln(a/b); no residual. Directed payments (HRIP, APAP, university, trauma) are pulled out first as a price component: SFY amounts converted to FFY as 0.75 x SFY t + 0.25 x SFY t+1 (FFY 2022 $2,749.0M, FFY 2024 $4,542.4M), split into an enrollment part and a per-member price part with the same L-weight formula; the non-directed-payment remainder is decomposed by group assuming directed payments are spread across groups in proportion to spending. Result: enrollment $-788M; mix $58M; directed-payment price $1,968M; other price and utilization $2,051M; total $3,288M.
measures.methodology: This splits the two-year rise in Kentucky Medicaid benefit spending into four parts. Spending and member counts are the federal CMS-64 figures MACPAC publishes; members are counted as full-year equivalents (average monthly enrollment). Only two eligibility groups are published on this basis for FFY 2024 (expansion adults and everyone else), so the mix part captures only that shift. Directed payments are the one price component that can be separated with public data; they are reported by state fiscal year and converted here, which assumes payments are spread evenly over the year, so that part is an estimate. Price changes other than directed payments (for example nursing home and waiver rate increases), changes in how much care members use, and changes in how sick the remaining members are cannot be separated with public data and are combined in the last part. After the continuous-coverage unwinding (April 2023 on), lower-cost members left first, so part of that last bar is acuity within groups, not price.
measures.proxyFor: price vs. utilization split by eligibility group (not publicly separable)
measures.comparability: CMS-64 (federal fiscal year, excludes administration and Medicaid-expansion CHIP) and DMS budget figures (state fiscal year, includes KCHIP) are on different bases; the directed-payment component is converted from SFY. notes: Item #10: 24 ledger rows (5 MCO, 6 waivers, 13 vendor/interagency). eMARS amounts for MCOs ($61.07B across the five, 2021-2026) are contract ceilings recorded at award and marked 'no funds added' on each amendment; they are lower than six years of reported premium revenue would suggest, so the UI should show annualValue (MCPAR premium revenue) as the money figure and the eMARS amount as the contract ceiling. MCO terms in eMARS end 12/31/2026; KRS 205.5321 extends them through 12/31/2028. Waiver 'value' is SFY 2025 services spending (DMS); the CHILD waiver (started Jan 2026) is not included. Status vocabulary: 'outcome defined' = a published target exists; 'no outcome defined' = no member or health outcome target in public documents (operational standards may still exist and are listed). No row is on/off track: no contract has both a published target and a published result for the same period. outcomeType separates health outcomes, process compliance, operational standards and deliverables. Item #13: headline uses CMS-64 (FFY 2022-2024, the years enrollment fell): +$3.29B with 4.8% fewer FYE members. Directed payments are the only separable price component; everything else is 'price and utilization together'. By-population detail exists only through FY 2023 (T-MSIS), when enrollment still rose; the two measures use different enrollment bases and do not reconcile. Never label rows waste, fraud or breach; MCPAR 'stateActions2024' reports compliance letters, corrective action plans and penalties as the state reported them.
